questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English-speaking country with courses that had opportunities for unique knowledge, that I wouldn't have been able to get at UCPH

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Bradley was very helpful in letting us know what we needed to do, and a lot of the other information was available on their website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Stop1 was always realy to answer any and all questions!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
* Colleges with meal services (picture Hogwarts); the more sociable option
* Student apartments (UniLodge, Scape); the more independent option

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Meal services at colleges. 
A big shared kitchen in Unilodge accomodations, where you could use all of their facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was a clear difference in cleanliness standards among the students living in the student apartments.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to fill out an excel sheet with your desired courses, and they require you to attatch a list of completed courses that would be necessary prerequisites. Be sure to check up on the prerequisites of your desired courses and have an english course description ready, so you don't get denied.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop1 and Bradley (international student contact person) were very helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got three out of foure of my top priorities; since the last was a laboratory course, it had an earlier deadline for application, which I was not made aware of. Is also had a quota and (understandably) filled up quite fast. If it's a necessary course for you to take, you are able to contact the university and ask for an exeption, which one of my friends was successful with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find more than your required number of courses, since it's not guaranteed that you can get your top priorities. Start your research early!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally, the academic level was a bit lower than that of UCPH (in the courses i enrolled in)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UniMelb, it's often times not just the final exam that will constitute your final grade, but also assignments and quizzes during the semester. This forces you to keep up with the lectures and reading list, which (for me at least) proved to be quite helpful, since I fould it easy to get distracted by exploring the amazing city and surrounding areas.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration
Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry
Frontiers in Human Disease
Australia in the Wine World

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration was an overall great course! The content was interesting and the lecturers' enthusiasm within their field of research was contagious. 
Australia in the Wine World was a very fun elective, which allowed me (a previous wine amateur) to learn so much about wines both from Australia and the "old world" of wine production.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's generally expensive to live in Melbourne. Remember to put aside money for weekend trips and maybe a longer trip in the mid semester break - there are so many must-see places in Australia!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The visa was more expensive than anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many different clubs for all different interests/hobbies/sports!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfers club!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Phillip Island, Great Ocean Road, Yarra Valley (wineries)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, since Melbourne has a very westernized culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Greeting the tram-/busdrivers and just a general interest in strangers' lives!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring warm clothes! It gets colder than expected. 
Sign up for the free frozen meals offered by UniMelb.
Relax and have fun; you're headed for (in my opinion) one of the best cities on earth!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Forcing me out of my comfort zone, both socially and academically; gives rise to a lot of maturation and invaluable experiences!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time zone differences to home are kind of challenging, especially in the first couple of weeks.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
